# Writing maths in your notes {#sec-writing-math}

If you take notes in Obsidian, Notion, Jupyter, Quarto or another Markdown-based tool, you can write formulas that look like the ones in this book. Almost all of these tools use the same notation, called **LaTeX** maths. You only need a small part of it.

## Inline and display formulas

| Tool | Formula inside a sentence | Formula on its own line |
|---------------------|---------------------|-------------------------|
| Obsidian, Quarto, Jupyter, many others | `$...$` | `$$...$$` |
| Notion | Equations from the `/` menu (inline or block) | Equation block from the `/` menu |

The LaTeX you type inside is the same in all of them. For example, typing

```markdown
The gross price is $p_{gross} = p_{net} \cdot (1 + t)$.
```

gives: The gross price is $p_{gross} = p_{net} \cdot (1 + t)$.

## The commands you need for this block

| You want | You type | You get |
|--------------------|----------------------------|-----------------|
| Multiplication dot | `3 \cdot 4`                 | $3 \cdot 4$ |
| Fraction           | `\frac{a}{b}`               | $\frac{a}{b}$ |
| Power              | `x^2`, `1.05^{12}`          | $x^2$, $1.05^{12}$ |
| Index (subscript)  | `K_0`, `p_{net}`            | $K_0$, $p_{net}$ |
| Square root, n-th root | `\sqrt{x}`, `\sqrt[3]{x}` | $\sqrt{x}$, $\sqrt[3]{x}$ |
| Percent sign       | `19\%`                      | $19\%$ |
| Approximately, not equal | `\approx`, `\neq`     | $\approx$, $\neq$ |
| Less or equal, greater or equal | `\leq`, `\geq` | $\leq$, $\geq$ |
| Text inside a formula | `\text{profit}`          | $\text{profit}$ |
| Sum                | `\sum_{t=1}^{n} x_t`        | $\sum_{t=1}^{n} x_t$ |
| Greek letters      | `\alpha`, `\Delta`, `\pi`   | $\alpha$, $\Delta$, $\pi$ |

Curly braces `{ }` group things: `1.05^12` gives $1.05^12$ (only the 1 is raised), while `1.05^{12}` gives $1.05^{12}$.

## A longer example

Several lines that line up at the `=` sign use an `aligned` block, with `&` before each `=` and `\\` at the end of each line:

```markdown
$$
\begin{aligned}
\text{price} &= 260 \cdot 1.40 \\
             &= 364
\end{aligned}
$$
```

$$
\begin{aligned}
\text{price} &= 260 \cdot 1.40 \\
             &= 364
\end{aligned}
$$

::: {.callout-tip}
## Is it worth it?
Typing formulas takes practice, and handwritten notes are just as good for learning. If you already take digital notes, though, a few commands from the table above go a long way. An AI assistant can also translate a formula you describe in words into LaTeX; check the result by looking at how it renders.
:::
